name: Brian Schatz
stance: Wants mandatory public disclosure of AI model capabilities and safeguards, including against autonomous loss of control, enforced by the FTC.

statements.text: The risks of AI are not theoretical — they are happening in real-time. Immediate risk requires immediate action.

Co-introduced the bipartisan AI Systems Transparency Act, requiring AI companies to disclose data practices and safeguards for child safety, cybersecurity, disaster risk and autonomous loss of control.
Our bill requires disclosures that help both consumers and evaluators understand both the capabilities of and risks.
If the risk of AI is anywhere near the level that it has been characterized to be, then we have an obligation to act on a bipartisan basis immediately.
I am still studying this but it's a reasonable start, and takes seriously the proposition that we need real proposals that can be enacted rapidly.
Led six senators in introducing the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal President Trump's executive order seeking to prevent states from regulating artificial intelligence.

Discouraging states from enacting common-sense regulation that protects people from potential AI harms is dangerous. Congress has a responsibility to get this technology right, but states must not be penalized for acting in the public interest in the meantime.

Co-signed letters to OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Anthropic, Meta, Luka, Character.AI and xAI asking them to commit to timely, consistent safety disclosures around model releases, warning that trouble with well-understood risks raises concerns about managing more complex ones.

Embracing the amazing possibilities of AI can’t come at the cost of leaving Americans vulnerable to its profound risks, which is exactly what this executive order does. Preventing states from enacting common-sense regulation that protects people from the very real harms of AI is absurd and dangerous. Congress has a responsibility to get this technology right – and quickly – but states must be allowed to act in the public interest in the meantime.
statements.outlet: Office of Sen. Schatz (via Capitol Releases)

statements.text: As the AI industry rapidly grows, it’s critical that we work to ensure the technology is safe for people to use and that companies are holding up their end of the bargain by following through on their safety commitments.

Led five lawmakers in a letter asking OpenAI CEO Sam Altman how the company would meet its public safety commitments, after whistleblower claims that it rushed safety testing of GPT-4o and barred employees from warning the public about risks.
